description: Different ways of doing a project - Plan A, Plan B - with what each would cost, take and risk. The planner. Import THIRTY-NINTH (needs user_projects)
notes: A project can hold several of these at once. That is the point: the alternatives are written down side by side rather than argued about from memory, and the one that was picked is recorded next to the ones that were not.

status carries 'rejected' deliberately. A rejected plan is KEPT, not deleted - 'we looked at this and said no' is exactly what you want in front of you when someone proposes it again three weeks later.
rating is 1-5 and is the person's own judgement. It carries the most weight in the ordering because it is the only field that knows things the others cannot - see config/plan-score.ts.
cost, duration_days, effort, risk and confidence are the trackable fields. Every one is optional: a half-filled plan still sorts, and an empty field counts as unknown rather than as bad.
The SCORE is not stored. It is computed from the fields and only ever compares a plan with its siblings, so storing it would be a number that goes stale the moment another plan is added.
project_id is TEXT holding the user_projects row id, as everywhere else in this app.

title.description: e.g. 'Plan A - do the floors first'. Primary field

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string. EVERY read filters on this

summary.description: What this plan actually is, in a sentence or two

cost.description: What it is expected to cost

currency.description: ISO code. Blank means the project's own

duration_days.description: How long it takes end to end

decided_at.description: When it was chosen or rejected

sample_data.title: Plan A — floors before the walls
